recipes.name: Coconut Chicken Stir Fry
ingredients_raw: 4 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, thinly sliced
0.5 teaspoon curry powder, or more to taste
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook and stir the cumin seeds in butter until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Stir chicken into the skillet with cumin seeds, and cook and stir until chicken is no longer pink in the center and juices run clear, 5 to 8 minutes. Drain any excess juices, if any.
Pour vegetable oil into skillet with chicken, and heat oil until sizzling.

Mix in onion, carrots, garlic, ginger, red pepper flakes, honey, ground cumin, cinnamon, curry powder, salt, and black pepper to the pan; cook until onions are translucent and carrots done, 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer until flavors have blended, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Chicken Stir Fry
raw_recipe.description: This coconut chicken stir fry is perfumed with an assortment of spices to make a dish that goes well over rice or pasta.

review.reviewBody: We enjoyed this very much. We used lite coconut milk. Next time we will add more than 1/2 t curry because we really like it.

A blend of delicious flavours. Delicate coconut, with a nice zing on the lips from the chilli pepper flakes. 
I whipped up this recipe for two in 45 minutes.

I substituted the cumin seeds with a 1/2 tsp. of cumin powder. I added half the chopped onions and half minced garlic in with it to give more flavour to the chicken. I cooked the chicken most of the way before adding the oil and veggies (tip: along with the carrots, I added broccoli crowns. It holds in the flavours really well!) 

For the spices I skipped the cinnamon, added an extra dash of pepper flakes, and upped the curry powder to 2 tsp. I also substituted the salt with lemon pepper then poured in the coconut milk right away so the flavours could blend as it simmered. 

5 stars, I couldn't believe how easy it was. Next time, I'll try fresh coriander/ cilantro garnish.
Yummy!

This smells heavenly! I made a few modifications, added 1/2 tsp of coriander, substituted freshly grated nutmeg for cinnamon (thought I had some but didn't so I had to improvise). Used scallions instead of onion and added snow peas for color and texture. Served over Basmati rice and sprinkled some chopped cilantro, mint and peanuts over the top.


I reduced the red pepper flake by 1/2, I love spice but my body doesn't. **Edited to add, I didn't use cumin seeds, couldn't find them at Publix, so I just used ground cumin with the butter and then again with the spice mixture added later**.

Letting this dish sit for a while before serving allowed the flavors to blend, and it was delicious. I was forced to make one change when I went to the pantry and realized I had used the coconut milk in another recipe. All I had was coconut Greek yogurt, so I added a 5.3 ounce container. It was the perfect amount of creamy goodness. When I make it in the future, I'll probably stick with the yogurt.

This is really good. Based on other comments I doubled all the seasonings (except the red peppers which I halved). I added a teaspoon of garam masala seasoning as well. I also let the dish simmer for about 25 minutes which really thickened it up and blended the flavors well. I'll definitely make this again, will likely add almond slivers and another vegetable to it.

I had to use up some coconut milk that I had opened, so I tried this. It was fantastic! I added more curry powder and 1-1/2 tsp of red pepper flakes were enough for me. I think that, instead of adding more curry powder, I would use curry paste because I thought it was a bit 'gritty'. Threw in some peas and cilantro at the end, as others suggested. Overall a great dish!

I love anything curry but I made adjustments. I did not use cumin seeds and used broccoli, purple onion and mushrooms because that’s what I had. I deleted the honey and used 1/2 cup of coconut aminos. I doubled the amount of curry and cut the hot peppers in half. I also thickened the sauce with arrowroot powder. It turned out great but I may try adding back the honey and using soy sauce because it was still a little too sweet for my taste.

Fantastic! only thing I did different is quadrupled the curry and halved the pepper flakes. I also doubled the sauce part simply because it seemed like I had a ton of chicken. I also added a corn starch slurry to thicken it and served over plain old minute rice.

I made this for dinner today after reading the reviews. So I added bell pepper, (and because I have little ppl eating), I only added 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes and 1 heaping tbsp honey. I seasoned my chicken (600 gr) with the salt, black pepper and ground cumin, all in 1 tsp (I didn't have cumin seeds). I love curry so I added 3 tsp curry powder and because I added the salt and pepper for my chicken I substitute the salty for fish sauce (I tbsp) and kept the 1 tsp ground cumin from the recipe (also the ground cinnamon). Another issue the coconut milk for the my amount of chicken and veggies I only added +/- 300 ml. I didn't have a chance to take a pic, it was that good!!!

Made it according to directions. I liked the cumin seeds in addition to ground cumin, it was very fragrant while cooking. However, when we ate it, it felt like it was lacking in depth of flavor and texture. I felt like I was eating curry that was just short of good. The following night we made chicken curry again, fried the cumin seeds, but added Mae Ploy red chili paste (has lemongrass), Mae Ploy green chili paste (already has ginger), with green and red bell peppers, green beans, carrots, coco milk, and added the honey and a dash of cayenne. Turned out to be more flavorful with heat level 4/10.

A tasty, healthy supper. I wanted more veggies, so in addition to the carrots and onion, I added a red pepper, yellow pepper, and two zucchinis. I also used leftover chicken rather than fresh (added it after the vegetables were getting soft). The adults and older kids enjoyed this, but the under-10 crowd didn't go for it.

My husband loved the spice. I’m not big on a lot of spice, so I cut the red pepper flakes down to 1.5 teaspoon. Next time I’ll do 1 teaspoon and he can add more. Luckily we are eating it with rice, so I’ll be fine. Definitely great flavor!
I like spicy, but the pepper flakes were too much. Otherwise very tasty.
This was ok, a little too much cumin for my liking. Probably will not make again
This was delicious! My picky teenagers loved it. My son even went back for seconds. I used frozen stir fry veggies instead of fresh carrots. I’m adding it into the regular dinner rotation.
Quick, easy and delicious.
Delicious! But somehow came out extra spicy. I doubled the curry powder and added chopped red bell pepper. Family loved it.
Made as per recipe (with basmati rice). Everyone thought it was great. This one will stay in my favorites.

loved this dish. 2 tsp of pepper flakes is spicy yo the lips. if you dont like the spice reduce to 1 tsp. I agree about missing a little flavor. I served with soy sauce and that made a great addition to the flavors. definitely would make again.

Added 2 yellow peppers after adding the coconut milk, added extra garlic, ginger and was heavy handed with the spices. Added a large handful of cilantro at the very end. Would consider adding pineapple to mix it up a bit. Will totally make it again.
